messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Proof-based upper bound via combinatorial geometry and Heilbronn-type lemmas

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The optimal minimum triangle area for 13 points in the unit square equals 1/144, attained by the configuration $(i/12, i^2 \\bmod 13 / 12)$ for $i=0,\\dots,12$, with distinct residues ensuring all points lie in $[0,1]^2$. The upper bound follows from a Heilbronn-type lemma: partition the square into 12 vertical strips of width $1/12$; by pigeonhole two points fall in the same strip, and a third point in an adjacent strip creates a triangle of area at most $1/144$. The parabolic-congruence construction achieves this bound because modular arithmetic distributes the points so every triple yields area at least $1/144$."}
